'''Édith Mourier''' (21 December 1920 - 19 December 2017)<ref>{{Cite web |title=matchID - Moteur de recherche des décès |url=https://deces.matchid.io/id/zsJLTeTJcVyG |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=deces.matchid.io}}</ref> was a French mathematician, specialising in [[probability theory]]. She is remembered in particular for the {{ill|Fortet–Mourier distance|de|Satz von Mourier}}, used to quantify the difference between two measurements.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last1=Baey |first1=Charlotte |last2=Bouaziz |first2=Olivier |last3=Croizat |first3=Barnabé |date=November 2025 |title=Newsletter Commission Parité (Novembre 2025), Laboratoire Paul Painlevé (Université de Lille) |url=https://math.univ-lille.fr/fileadmin/user_upload/pages_pros/charlotte_baey/newsletter_nov25.pdf |access-date=5 March 2026 |publisher=Laboratoire Paul Painlevé |language=fr}}</ref>

In 1952, Mourier was appointed director of research at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS). After defending her doctoral thesis, Mourier was appointed director of research at the CNRS until 1956 when she became a lecturer at the [[University of Poitiers]], then at the [[University of Paris]] from 1967 to 1987. For the remainder of her career she was active in the LPMA laboratory.<ref name=":2" />

== Biography ==

=== Early life and education ===
Édith Marguerite Pauline Mourier was born on 21 December 1920 in [[Cherbourg]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=France |first=Décès en |title=Mme MOURIER Edith Marguerite Pauline - Décès en France - Registre des personnes décédées en France depuis 1970 à 2026 |url=https://www.deces-en-france.fr/resultats/23656326-mourier-edith-marguerite-pauline |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=www.deces-en-france.fr |language=fr}}</ref> She studied mathematics at the [[Sorbonne University|Sorbonne]].<ref name=":2" />

Little is known of her early life or family but in 1944 she was in Paris and had graduated in mathematics. Records from the [[Université de Poitiers]] show that she held a position at the École Normale for the 1944-1945 academic year.<ref name=":0"/>

=== Career ===
After earning her bachelor's degree, she joined the [[Institut Henri Poincaré|institut Henri-Poincaré]] where she collaborated with a small group of researchers working on [[probability theory]],<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Claire Berthelemy |last2=Gabriel Jaquemet |date=2026-01-28 |title=Dans quelles écoles ont été formées les 72 scientifiques dont les noms vont orner la tour Eiffel ? |url=https://www.leparisien.fr/etudiant/etudes/ecoles/universite-de-paris-ens-medecine-dou-viennent-les-72-scientifiques-dont-les-noms-vont-orner-la-tour-eiffel-NFQ32TZMIRDITKDZOPS5RUHVLM.php |access-date=2026-01-31 |website=leparisien.fr |language=fr-FR}}</ref> a field of mathematical research which was somewhat neglected in France at the time.<ref name=":2" /> 

In 1948, Mourier spent some time at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where [[Jerzy Neyman]] attracted French probabilists. Although [[Lucien Le Cam]] and [[Michel Loève]] reamined there, Mourier soon returned to France<ref name=":0"/>

Mourier became a researcher at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (French National Centre for Scientific Research) (CNRS) in 1945.<ref name=":2" /> At this time, she took part in an informal reading group on statistics with [[Lucien Le Cam|Lucien de Cam]] and {{Ill|Colette Cassignol|lt=Colette Rothschild|fr|Colette Cassignol}}. <ref>{{Cite journal |last=Yang |first=Grace L. |date=1999-05-01 |title=A conversation with Lucien Le Cam |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistical-science/volume-14/issue-2/A-conversation-with-Lucien-Le-Cam/10.1214/ss/1009212249.full |journal=Statistical Science |volume=14 |issue=2 |doi=10.1214/ss/1009212249 |issn=0883-4237}}</ref>   

In 1952, Mourier was appointed director of research at CNRS after defending her [[doctoral thesis]] on "Random elements in a [[Banach space]]''"'' ({{Langx|fr|Éléments aléatoires dans un espace de Banach}}).<ref name=":2" /> This work generalises the [[law of large numbers]] relating to random points to function spaces (Banach spaces), known as the {{ill|Fortet–Mourier distance|de|Satz von Mourier}} after Mourier and her PhD supervisor and colleague [[Robert Fortet]].<ref name=":2" /> The {{ill|Mourier theorem|de|Satz von Mourier (Maßtheorie)}} for the equality of the cylindrical and Borel σ-algebras on separable Banach spaces is also named after her.

After leaving CNRS, Mourier became a lecturer (''maître de conférences'') at the [[University of Poitiers]] from 1956 to 1967, then at the [[University of Paris]] from 1967 to 1987, where in particular she was active in the LPMA laboratory ({{Ill|Laboratoire de probabilités et modèles aléatoires|fr}}), collaborating with Robert Fortet and the evolving [[Jacques Neveu]].<ref name=":2" />

She remained at the LPNA for the next 20 years, that is until the end of her career. She continued to maintain an interest in telecommunications, investigating signal detection in the presence of noise and also embarking on the definition of [[white noise]].<ref name=":2" />

=== Death ===
Édith Mourier died age 96 on 19 December 2017 in the apartment on Rue Sarrette in the [[14th arrondissement of Paris]] where she had lived for the past 60 years. <ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Her name continues to be associated with the Fortet–Mourier distance, a metric used in [[probability theory]] to quantify the difference between two [[probability measure]]s based an the evaluation of the gap between their bounded [[Lipschitz continuity|Lipschitz continuity functions]]. She was also an important contributor to developing a marriage between [[random variable]]s and complete [[Normed vector space|normed space]]s.<ref name=":0" /> She produced an extension of the [[Glivenko–Cantelli theorem]] in 1953.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fortet |first=R. |last2=Mourier |first2=E. |date=1953 |title=Convergence de la répartition empirique vers la répartition théorique |url=https://www.numdam.org/item/?id=ASENS_1953_3_70_3_267_0 |journal=Annales scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure |language=fr |volume=70 |issue=3 |pages=267–285 |doi=10.24033/asens.1013 |issn=1873-2151}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

== Commemoration ==
In 2026, Édith Mourier was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was conceived by a student and tour guide named Bernard Rigaud<ref name="rigaud">{{Cite web |title=The Hypatia project: engraving the names of 72 women scientists on the Eiffel Tower |url=https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/news/hypatia-project-engraving-names-72-women-scientists-eiffel-tower |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Sorbonne Université |language=en}}</ref> and it was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of [[Femmes et Sciences]] and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref>{{citation |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref>[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-02-22</ref><ref name=":1">{{citation |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-02-03 |language=en}}</ref>
